read: Adoption vs wrong-peer count: 1-peer 0.9714, 2-peer 0.9714, 4-peer 1.0. The curve is essentially flat from one peer onward (1-vs-2 and 2-vs-4 McNemars below), confirming from the size axis what #172 found from the majority axis: the imaging cascade saturates at a single confident wrong peer, and adding more peers (up to four) recruits essentially no additional adoption. It is a single-peer, not a graded-majority, effect.
